title: Locale aware sorting with Intl.Collator
when: Names, titles or files must sort alphabetically the way people expect: accents in place, case ignored, item 2 before item 10.
prompt:
Goal: Text sorting and comparison through cached Intl.Collator instances configured for the user locale and the data.
Steps:
1. Create once: const collator = new Intl.Collator(locale, { sensitivity: "base", numeric: true }); sort with collator.compare.
2. numeric: true orders "file 2" before "file 10"; caseFirst only when the domain needs it.
3. Accent and case insensitive equality: compare(a, b) === 0 with sensitivity "base".
4. Sort a copy ([...items] or toSorted) with an id tie breaker for stable order.
5. Pass the user locale; some languages order letters differently (Swedish puts a with ring after z).
6. Build alphabet index headings (A, B, C) by comparing first letters with the same collator.
Quality bar:
- Accented names sit next to their base letter.
- Numbers inside names sort by value.
- Order is stable across reloads.
Pitfalls:
- Default sort(), which orders by code units (Z before a, accents last).
- toLowerCase comparisons that ignore locale.
- A new collator or localeCompare with options per comparison in hot loops.
Verify:
- [ ] One cached collator.
- [ ] Tests with accents, case and numbers.
- [ ] Shared arrays not mutated.
- [ ] Tie breaker present.
Output: js/sort.js exporting the collator helpers used by lists and tables.

examples.input: a lista de alunos coloca "Álvaro" depois do "Zeca"
examples.output: Intl.Collator("pt-BR", { sensitivity: "base", numeric: true }) cached, sort copies with id tie breaker
